name: WooCommerce
one_liner: Free WordPress e-commerce plugin whose REST API lets external systems read and write store data.
auth_notes: Consumer key and secret pairs generated per WordPress user in WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API; sent via HTTP Basic Auth over HTTPS, or OAuth 1.0a one-legged over HTTP (not an OAuth 2 flow).
access_notes: Store admin generates Consumer Key and Consumer Secret in WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API; the core plugin is described as free. Consumer Secret is shown only once. Legacy REST API needs a separate free plugin.

buildability.rationale: Self-serve free REST API with key auth and webhooks, but each merchant's self-hosted store needs its own admin-generated keys, and the docs do not state endpoint count, sandbox, or rate limits.

identity.quote: The WooCommerce REST API connects your store to external systems and services.

auth.quote: You may use HTTP Basic Auth by providing the REST API Consumer Key as the username and the REST API Consumer Secret as the password.

access.quote: This documentation is about the free, core WooCommerce plugin, for which support is provided in our community forums on WordPress.org.
Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API.

api_surface.quote: The orders API allows you to create, view, update, and delete individual, or a batch, of orders.

mcp.quote: The MCP implementation in WooCommerce is currently in developer preview.
With the MCP Adapter plugin, AI clients can discover and run these store operations through the Model Context Protocol (MCP),

needs_human_reason: Self-hosted per-store REST API: each merchant must generate keys in their own admin; no sandbox, endpoint count, or rate limits documented on fetched pages; MCP integration is developer preview.
